items.title: Manny Albam interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: so I sold it to Georgie Auld when I joined the band

ctx.x: Then your mother comes in and cleans up and you’re going like where is —

Right. What happened to the second trombone part, my God, oh it’s under the bed. And that’s the way it looked to me. I wrote about four or five charts like that. I wrote an arrangement, I think the third arrangement I wrote was an arrangement for a singer on Muggsy’s band on “The Man I Love.” And ultimately Muggsy didn’t buy it and so I sold it to Georgie Auld when I joined the band for his singer. What else? Oh, Herbie Fields, by that time he was in the Army. He had a band in Atlantic City and I wrote a chart…
What was a chart going for back then?
